examples.en: I am barely getting by on my salary.
The shop has no customers, so it is barely hanging on.
I scraped together my tuition with part-time jobs.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 적자 속에서도 근근이 문을 열고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is barely staying open despite running at a loss.

examples.ko: 근근이 모은 돈을 병원비로 다 썼어요.
examples.en: I spent all the money I had barely saved up on hospital bills.

examples.ko: 할머니는 작은 밭에서 나온 것으로 근근이 먹고 사셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother barely got by on what came from her small field.

explain: '겨우', '간신히'와 비슷하지만 '근근이'는 어려운 형편에서 힘들게 이어 가는 모습에 많이 써요. '살다, 버티다, 모으다, 이어 가다'와 잘 어울려요. '합격선을 근근이 넘다'처럼 한 번에 아슬아슬하게 해내는 일에는 '간신히'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I barely keep my life going through farming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 형편에서 힘들게 계속하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes continuing with difficulty in hard circumstances.

phrases.en: I scraped together my allowance and bought shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금씩 어렵게 돈을 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saving money little by little with difficulty.

phrases.en: I barely arrived on time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근근이'보다 쓰임이 넓고 일상에서 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Wider in use than 근근이 and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It is similar to '겨우' and '간신히', but '근근이' leans toward continuing with difficulty in hard circumstances. It goes well with '살다', '버티다', '모으다' and '이어 가다'. For barely pulling off a single thing, like just clearing a passing score, '간신히' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The market the day before a holiday is as chaotic as a bazaar.
On the first day of the sale, the store turned into a zoo.

examples.ko: 사람이 너무 많아서 역 앞이 도떼기시장 같았어요.
examples.en: There were so many people that the area in front of the station was a madhouse.
During breaks, the classroom turns into a madhouse.

examples.ko: 도떼기시장에서 물건을 사려면 큰 소리로 말해야 해요.
examples.en: To buy things in a chaotic market, you have to speak loudly.
Yesterday's event hall was a madhouse, so I was overwhelmed.

explain: 사람이 많고 시끄러워서 정신없는 장소나 상황을 시장에 빗대어 말해요. 시장 자체보다 행사장, 교실, 매장 같은 곳에 비유로 쓸 때가 많아요. 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The subway station at rush hour is like a chaotic market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '같다'를 붙여서 정신없는 장소를 비유로 말할 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 같다, it is the easiest way to compare a hectic place to this market.
phrases.en_equiv: to be like a chaotic market

phrases.example: 아이들이 뛰어다녀서 교실은 도떼기시장이 따로 없어요.
phrases.en: With the kids running around, the classroom is a total zoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정말 그 모습 그대로다'라는 느낌을 더해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feeling of 'it is exactly that', for emphasis.

phrases.en: The event hall was chaotic from the start.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소의 전체적인 느낌을 설명할 때 '분위기'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '분위기' to describe the overall feel of a place.

explain_en: It compares a crowded, noisy, chaotic place or situation to a market. It is often used figuratively for event halls, classrooms or stores rather than markets themselves. It carries a slightly negative tone.

en: to be left unpaid; to have money not repaid

examples.en: I never got back the money I lent my friend.
My wages weren't paid, so life is really hard.

examples.ko: 외상값을 떼이지 않으려면 계약서를 써야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid not getting paid, you should write a contract.

examples.ko: 돈을 떼인 사람들이 사무실 앞에 모였어요.
examples.en: People who were never paid gathered in front of the office.

examples.ko: 보증금을 떼일까 봐 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I can't sleep for fear of losing my deposit.

examples.ko: 한 번 떼이고 나니까 이제 돈은 안 빌려줘요.
examples.en: After getting burned once, I don't lend money anymore.

explain: 받을 돈을 못 받았을 때 피해 본 사람이 쓰는 말이에요. 돈을 안 주는 쪽은 '떼먹다'를 쓰고, 보통 '돈을 떼이다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The shop owner didn't get paid for the goods sold on credit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받을 외상값을 못 받았을 때 피해 본 쪽이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said by the victim who failed to receive money owed on credit.
phrases.en_equiv: to be stiffed on a tab

phrases.example: 이번에는 돈을 떼이지 않게 계약서를 썼어요.
phrases.en: This time I wrote a contract so I wouldn't get cheated out of the money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 돈을 안전하게 받기 위한 조심을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it expresses taking care to be paid safely.

phrases.en: I'm worried my landlord won't return my deposit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌려받아야 할 큰돈을 못 받는 걱정에 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in worries about not getting a large sum back.

explain_en: Passive, you are the victim whose money is not repaid. This is what the victim says when they can't collect money owed to them. The person who doesn't pay is described with '떼먹다', and the usual phrase is '돈을 떼이다'.

examples.en: At the typhoon news, people stockpiled ramyeon.
The supermarket has no toilet paper because of panic buying.
Panic buying harms other people.

examples.ko: 물건이 부족해질까 봐 사재기하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people hoard because they fear a shortage.

examples.ko: 가격이 오르기 전에 사재기에 나선 사람들이 있었어요.
examples.en: Some people started stockpiling before prices rose.
Don't hoard; buy only what you need.

explain: 필요 이상으로 많이 사서 쌓아 두는 것이라 보통 좋지 않은 느낌으로 말해요. 뉴스에서는 태풍, 가격 인상, 물건 부족 같은 상황에서 자주 나와요. 동사로는 '사재기하다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: Some people were panic buying masks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '사재기'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding 하다 to the noun 사재기.

phrases.example: 정부가 사재기를 막으려고 구매 수량을 제한했어요.
phrases.en: The government limited purchase amounts to prevent panic buying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing you often hear in the news.

phrases.en: The news said panic buying is severe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사재기가 사회에서 크게 나타나는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when panic buying shows up widely in society.

explain_en: It means buying far more than you need and piling it up, so it carries a negative tone. In the news it appears often with typhoons, price hikes and shortages. The verb form is '사재기하다'.

en: penniless person; person who has lost everything

examples.en: His business failed and he became penniless overnight.
He came up to Seoul with absolutely nothing.
I almost lost everything because of stocks.
Once I was left penniless, my friends disappeared too.
Before payday I'm practically broke.

examples.ko: 잘못된 투자로 재산을 날려 알거지가 된 사람 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about a man who lost his fortune in a bad investment and ended up penniless.

explain: 가진 것이 하나도 없는 사람을 말해요. '빈털터리'와 비슷하지만 '거지'가 들어가서 더 센 표현이에요. 월급날 전에 '나 알거지야'처럼 과장해서 농담으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 주식으로 돈을 다 잃고 알거지가 됐어요.
phrases.en: I lost all my money in stocks and became penniless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재산을 모두 잃은 결과를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used for the result of losing all one's property.

phrases.example: 월급을 다 써서 지금은 알거지나 다름없어요.
phrases.en: I've spent my whole salary, so I'm practically broke now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정말 거지는 아니지만 거의 그런 상태라고 과장해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to exaggerate that one is almost, though not literally, penniless.
phrases.en_equiv: to be as good as penniless

phrases.en: I heard he was scammed and ended up in a penniless state.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신세'가 붙어서 처지가 딱하다는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 신세 gives a feel of a pitiable situation.

explain_en: It means a person with absolutely nothing. It is similar to '빈털터리' but stronger because it contains '거지' (beggar). People also joke with it, saying '나 알거지야' before payday.

en: to stagnate; to be stalled; to be congested (traffic)

examples.en: The roads get congested at rush hour.

examples.ko: 우리 회사의 성장이 몇 년째 정체되었어요.
examples.en: Our company's growth has been stagnant for years.
The traffic jam lasted so long that I was very late.
Exports have been stagnant for months, so I am worried.
I want to change the stagnant mood.
Cars are backed up because of the snow.

explain: 길이 막힐 때는 '막히다'가 더 일상적이고, '정체되다'는 뉴스의 교통 정보에서 자주 나와요. 일이나 경제가 앞으로 나아가지 않을 때도 써요. 반대로 빠르게 나아갈 때는 '성장하다', '발전하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I waited for an hour on the congested road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 많아서 움직이지 않는 길을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a road where cars are barely moving.

phrases.en: The economy is stagnating these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행되는 상태를 말하는 모양으로, 경제나 일에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This progressive form describes an ongoing state, and it also works for the economy or work.

phrases.example: 오늘은 길이 정체되지 않아서 빨리 왔어요.
phrases.en: The road wasn't congested today, so I got here fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막히지 않고 잘 움직인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means traffic is moving well without a jam.

explain_en: For roads, '막히다' is more everyday, and '정체되다' appears often in news traffic reports. It also describes work or the economy that is not moving forward. When things move ahead quickly, you say '성장하다' or '발전하다'.

p.n: Grammatical either way, but 정체되다 sounds more natural for traffic.

t90.ax: I want to change the stagnant mood.

examples.ko: 여름에는 바다에서 계절풍이 불어와 비가 많이 와요.
examples.en: In summer, seasonal winds blow in from the sea and bring a lot of rain.

examples.ko: 계절풍 때문에 여름과 겨울의 바람 방향이 달라요.
examples.en: Because of the monsoon, the wind direction differs between summer and winter.
We learned about the monsoon climate in geography class.
Our country is strongly affected by the seasonal winds.

examples.ko: 겨울 계절풍은 차갑고 건조해서 피부가 트요.
examples.en: The winter monsoon is cold and dry, so skin gets chapped.

examples.ko: 계절풍을 이용해서 옛날 배들이 먼 바다를 건넜어요.
examples.en: In the old days, ships crossed distant seas by using the seasonal winds.

explain: 계절에 따라 부는 방향이 바뀌는 바람이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '바람'이나 '장마'라고 많이 하고, '계절풍'은 지리 수업이나 날씨 설명에서 자주 나와요. 외래어 '몬순'도 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 이 지역은 계절풍 기후라서 여름에 비가 많아요.
phrases.en: This region has a monsoon climate, so it rains a lot in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절풍의 영향을 받는 기후를 말하며 지리 수업에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A climate shaped by seasonal winds; common in geography class.

phrases.en: In winter the seasonal wind blows from the north.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 오는 방향을 함께 넣어서 설명할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Good for explaining along with the direction the wind comes from.

phrases.example: 몬순 때문에 여름에 비가 많이 와요.
phrases.en: Because of the monsoon, it rains a lot in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 외래어로, 뉴스와 수업에서 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword with the same meaning, used in news and lessons too.

explain_en: It is wind whose direction changes with the seasons. In daily talk people say '바람' or '장마', while '계절풍' mostly appears in geography lessons and weather explanations. The loanword '몬순' (monsoon) is used too.

examples.en: The plane is flying steadily at high altitude.
During a high-altitude flight, you can look down on the clouds out the window.

examples.ko: 요즘 물가가 고공 행진을 계속하고 있어요.
examples.en: Prices have kept soaring these days.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 고공 점프로 관중을 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: The athlete amazed the crowd with a high-flying jump.

examples.ko: 고공 작업을 할 때는 안전 장비가 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: Safety gear is a must when you work at great heights.

examples.ko: 고공 낙하 훈련을 받는 모습을 뉴스에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw on the news people doing high-altitude parachute training.

explain: 높은 하늘이나 아주 높은 곳을 말하고, 반대말은 '저공'이에요. 뉴스에서는 물가나 인기 같은 숫자가 계속 높을 때 '고공 행진'이라고 비유해서 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 드라마는 시청률 고공 행진을 이어 가고 있어요.
phrases.en: That drama's ratings keep staying sky-high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물가, 주가, 시청률처럼 높은 수치가 계속 유지되거나 오를 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 실제로 걷거나 날아가는 뜻은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used mostly in news when a high figure like prices, stocks or ratings keeps rising or stays high. It has nothing to do with actually marching or flying.

explain_en: It means the high sky or a very high place, and its opposite is '저공' (low altitude). In the news, '고공 행진' is a common figure of speech for numbers like prices or popularity staying high.

t90.ax: Prices have kept soaring these days.

examples.en: Cabbage grown in the cool highlands of Gangwon-do tastes good.

examples.ko: 고랭지 배추는 여름에도 시원한 곳에서 자라요.
examples.en: Highland cabbage grows in a place that is cool even in summer.

examples.ko: 올여름 비가 많이 와서 고랭지 채소 값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot this summer, so highland vegetable prices went up.

examples.ko: 고랭지로 유명한 이 마을에서는 감자도 많이 키워요.
examples.en: This village, famous as a cool highland area, grows a lot of potatoes too.

examples.ko: 고랭지 농업은 날씨에 영향을 크게 받아요.
examples.en: Highland farming is greatly affected by the weather.
Cool highlands are high up, so they stay cool even in summer.

explain: 높은 곳에 있어서 여름에도 서늘한 지역을 말하고, 뉴스나 마트에서 '고랭지 배추', '고랭지 무', '고랭지 감자'처럼 채소 이름 앞에 붙여 많이 써요. 여름 채소 값 소식에서 자주 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Highland vegetables are popular in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마트와 뉴스에서 가장 자주 만나는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing you most often meet in stores and the news.

phrases.en: It is a village where highland farming is developed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서늘한 높은 지역에서 짓는 농사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to farming done in high, cool areas.

phrases.en: This radish was grown in a highland area.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고랭지'에 조사 '에서'를 붙여 어디서 자랐는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle 에서 tells where the crop grew.
phrases.en_equiv: to grow in a cool highland

explain_en: High, cool mountain area used for farming (고랭지 배추) It refers to an area that stays cool even in summer because it is high up. In the news and at supermarkets it is attached to vegetable names, as in '고랭지 배추', '고랭지 무' and '고랭지 감자'. You often hear it in reports on summer vegetable prices.

t90.ax: Highland farming is greatly affected by the weather.

examples.en: In the Paleozoic era, trilobites lived in the sea.
The era after the Paleozoic is the Mesozoic.
I looked at Paleozoic fossils at the museum.

examples.ko: 고생대 말에 큰 변화가 있었다고 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned that there was a big change at the end of the Paleozoic.
They say this rock was formed in the Paleozoic era.
In science class we compared the Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras.

explain: 지구의 역사를 나눌 때 쓰는 말로 '고생대, 중생대, 신생대' 순서로 외우면 쉬워요. 학교 과학 시간이나 박물관에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '고생대에는', '고생대 화석'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I saw Paleozoic fossils at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박물관이나 과학 시간에 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in museums and science class.

phrases.en: In the Paleozoic era, many fish lived in the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시대에 있었던 일을 설명할 때 조사 '에는'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 에는 to describe what happened in that era.

phrases.example: 고생대 생물은 지금과 모양이 많이 달라요.
phrases.en: Paleozoic creatures look very different from today's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시대에 살던 생물을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to living things from that era.

explain_en: It is used to divide Earth's history, and it is easy to remember in the order 고생대, 중생대, 신생대 (Paleozoic, Mesozoic, Cenozoic). It appears often in school science classes and museums. It is usually used as '고생대에는' or '고생대 화석'.

en: to shine down; to glare down; to blaze down

examples.en: In midsummer the sun blazes down on the yard.

examples.ko: 햇볕이 너무 내리쬐니까 모자를 쓰고 가세요.
examples.en: The sun is beating down so hard, so wear a hat when you go.

examples.ko: 창문으로 아침 햇살이 내리쬐는 방이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like a room where the morning sun shines in through the window.

examples.ko: 뜨겁게 내리쬐던 해가 지고 나서 시원해졌어요.
examples.en: It got cool after the sun that had been glaring down set.

examples.ko: 해가 계속 내리쬐서 땀이 많이 났어요.
examples.en: The sun kept beating down, so I sweated a lot.

examples.ko: 가을 햇살이 따뜻하게 내리쬘 때 산책하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to take a walk when the autumn sun shines down warmly.

explain: 주로 해, 햇볕, 햇살이 주어로 와요. 그냥 빛이 들어오는 건 '비치다'라고 하고, 위에서 강하게 쏟아지는 느낌일 때 '내리쬐다'를 써요. 더운 날씨 이야기에서 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: At midday the sun beats down strongly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 위에서 강하게 쏟아질 때 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요. 더운 날씨 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural phrase when the sun pours down strongly. Fits talk about hot weather.

phrases.example: 내리쬐는 햇볕 아래에서 오래 걷지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't walk for long under the beating sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형이에요. 뜨거운 햇볕을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun. Used to describe hot sunshine.

phrases.en: I worked in a field under the scorching sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뙤약볕'은 여름의 아주 뜨거운 볕이에요. 더위를 더 강하게 말하고 싶을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '뙤약볕' is very hot summer sunshine. Use it to stress the heat more strongly.

explain_en: Strong, hot sun beating down (한여름 뜨거운 햇볕이 마당에 쨍쨍 내리쬐어요.) The subject is mostly the sun, sunlight or sunshine. For light that simply comes in, you say '비치다'; '내리쬐다' is for sunlight pouring down strongly from above. It comes up a lot when talking about hot weather.

t90.ax: In midsummer the sun blazes down on the yard.

en: to overflow; to brim; to spill

examples.en: During the rainy season, the river overflows.
The bathtub overflowed and the floor got wet.
The market is overflowing with people's energy.

examples.ko: 눈물이 넘쳐흐를 것 같아서 고개를 숙였어요.
examples.en: I lowered my head because tears seemed about to spill over.
His words brimmed with confidence.
Be careful that the soup doesn't spill over.

explain: '넘치다'에 흘러내리는 느낌이 더해진 말이에요. 물뿐 아니라 활기, 자신감, 감정이 가득 차서 겉으로 드러날 때도 써요. '흐르다'가 '르 불규칙'이라서 '넘쳐흘러요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: The cup is small, so the water overflows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현재 상황을 말하는 해요체 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite present-tense form describing what's happening now.

phrases.en: I saw the water overflowing from the dam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: That player is brimming with confidence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물뿐 아니라 감정이나 기운이 가득할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe feelings or energy that are abundant, not only water.

explain_en: It is '넘치다' with an added sense of flowing down. Besides water, it is used when energy, confidence or emotion is so full that it shows. Because '흐르다' is a '르' irregular verb, it becomes '넘쳐흘러요'.

examples.en: I wash fruit that has been sprayed with pesticide thoroughly.
The farmer is spraying pesticide on the field.
I bought vegetables grown without pesticide.
They say bees are decreasing because of pesticides.
The pesticide smell was strong, so I closed the window.
I visited a farm that doesn't use pesticides.

explain: '농약을 치다', '농약을 뿌리다'처럼 말하고, 마트에서는 '무농약', '저농약' 표시를 볼 수 있어요. 벌레를 없애는 약은 '살충제', 풀을 없애는 약은 '제초제'라고 해요.

phrases.en: They spray pesticide in the orchard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뿌리다'와 같은 뜻으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the same meaning as 뿌리다.

phrases.en: I bought pesticide-free vegetables.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마트 표시에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word often seen on supermarket labels.

phrases.en: There is a pesticide smell from the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냄새를 말할 때 '농약 냄새'로 합쳐 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combine it with 냄새 to talk about the smell.

explain_en: People say '농약을 치다' or '농약을 뿌리다', and in supermarkets you will see labels like '무농약' and '저농약'. Medicine to kill insects is '살충제' and to kill weeds is '제초제'.

examples.ko: 이 집은 단열이 잘 돼서 겨울에도 따뜻해요.
examples.en: This house is well insulated, so it's warm even in winter.

examples.ko: 단열재를 바꾸고 나서 난방비가 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: After we replaced the insulation material, our heating bill dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 오래된 건물은 창문 단열이 약한 편이에요.
examples.en: Old buildings tend to have weak window insulation.

examples.ko: 이 단열재는 실내 온도 유지에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This insulation material helps keep the indoor temperature steady.

examples.ko: 문틈에 단열 테이프를 붙였더니 훨씬 덜 추워요.
examples.en: I put insulating tape on the door gap, and it's much less cold now.
I heard insulation matters in summer too.

explain: '단열이 잘되다/안 되다', '단열재', '단열 공사'처럼 써요. 겨울 추위만 막는 게 아니라 여름에 바깥 열이 들어오는 것도 줄여 줘서 냉난방비와 관련해 자주 나와요. 비슷한 '보온'은 따뜻함을 유지한다는 쪽에 가까워요.

phrases.en: I put insulation material in the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열을 막아 주는 재료를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the material that blocks heat.

phrases.example: 단열이 안 돼서 겨울에 너무 추워요.
phrases.en: The insulation is poor, so it's very cold in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이 춥거나 더운 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain why a house is too cold or too hot.

phrases.en: We're doing insulation work next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 고치는 일에서 자주 듣는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard when talking about home renovation.

explain_en: It is used in phrases like '단열이 잘되다/안 되다', '단열재' and '단열 공사'. It does not only keep winter cold out but also reduces heat coming in during summer, so it often comes up with heating and cooling costs. The similar word '보온' is closer to keeping warmth in.
